name: Aurindunnum
description: Soaring in the skies, the capital city of the autumn elves floats above the Republic’s northern expanse. A blend of city and fortress, its autumnal glow, waterfalls, and spires are shaped by both tangible materials and unique illusion magic turned solid by intricate rituals. This magic allows the city to float amidst clouds, showcasing unique structures like levitating staircases and the orbiting spheres of light that brighten its nights, as well as granting all its residents illusory wings that allow flight. To shield Aurindunnum, robust abjuration wards stand, and countless air elementals are bound for its defense. Once in ruins, King Sundaryll regained hope when he fell in love with Anariel during the Kemet Invasion. Seeing the Republic as a chance for rebirth, and with the assistance of Archmage Avelum and High Cardinal Taram, the city was revitalized. However, challenges persist. The Cult of Shadow Wing often makes it a target of their assaults, and the Empire sees the airborne fortress as a threat, especially because of its alignment with the Republic. Yet, the gravest threat is internal, as Prince Quizzarian, Sundaryll’s younger brother, both brilliant and mad, is always working on plans to take the throne from his brother. Quizzarian plans go from harmless pranks to dangerous gambits to undermine Sundaryll. Whether it’s entrapping the King in a maze, magically enhancing monsters, breaking Sundaryll’s scepter and hiding the parts, or unleashing a plague with one unique cure, Quizzarian’s actions are always wrapped in riddles and intricate traps. His goal? To prove his intellectual superiority. Further complicating matters, Sundaryll must lead monthly ventures into the Penumbral Plane to gather energy from aberrations and emoguns. This energy sustains Aurindunnum’s defenses and keeps it airborne. Joined by Anariel and the mystical knights, riding Stormbirds of the god Aibidh, they are often seeking mercenaries and adventurers to help with specific threats or tasks during these missions.
